_description: Audit of src/app/sitemap.ts against the real route inventory (seo/site-route-inventory.json), plus the contract going forward.

audit.onlyCanonicalIndexableUrlsEnter: YES for everything already in the routes[] array - no alias, query-param, or duplicate URL was found entering the sitemap.
audit.aliasesExcluded: YES - the calculator catalog's 34 non-live candidate slugs never enter ALL_TOOL_SLUGS (the sitemap's own source), so they can't leak in.
audit.mergedJourneyIdsExcluded: YES, correctly - JOURNEY_ROWS (the sitemap's source) is JOURNEYS.map(...), which never includes the 5 MERGED_INTO entries. Verified: the 5 merged/noindex journey pages have zero sitemap entries.
audit.noindexUrlsLeaking: NO leaks found in what's currently listed - the one family that IS noindex (journey-merged) is correctly absent.
audit.allCalculatorsPresent: YES - /calculators + all 43 live calculator slugs + 2 utility tool slugs, via ALL_TOOL_SLUGS (verified in every prior calculator batch this session, re-confirmed this round).
audit.abTestDetailsPresent: NO - CONFIRMED BUG, fixed this round. /lab/ab-testing/library and all 211 /lab/ab-testing/library/{slug} pages were entirely absent from routes[] before this fix, despite being real, live, indexable, metadata-complete pages (confirmed by two independent audit passes this round).
audit.journeyDetailsPresent: YES - all 255 live journeys via JOURNEY_ROWS.map(...).
audit.blogArticlesPresent: YES - all 5 EN-only articles via getAllBlogPosts('en').map(...), correctly emitting only the EN URL with no alternates block (blog has no TR counterpart).
audit.labProductPagesPresent: YES - /lab/ab-testing and /lab/dashboard-builder are both static entries in routes[].

fixAppliedThisRound.change: Added "/lab/ab-testing/library" as a static entry, and ...ALL_AB_TEST_SLUGS.map((slug) => `/lab/ab-testing/library/${slug}`) as a spread entry, mirroring the exact existing pattern already used for ALL_TOOL_SLUGS (calculators) and JOURNEY_ROWS (journeys) two lines above/below it in the same file.
fixAppliedThisRound.riskLevel: very low - additive only, same tested pattern reused verbatim, no existing entry touched, verified with tsc/build.
fixAppliedThisRound.notPushed: Committed locally per this round's explicit no-deploy instruction; not pushed to origin.

familySegmentation.reasoning: Total entries after the fix: roughly (9 static top-level + 1 calculator-index + 45 calculator/utility + 1 ab-test-library-index + 211 ab-test-library-detail + 255 journey-library-detail) x2 languages, plus 5 EN-only blog articles = comfortably under 5,000 URLs (Google's per-sitemap soft limit is 50,000 URLs / 50MB uncompressed). A single sitemap.xml stays well within limits - splitting into a sitemap index + per-family sitemaps would be pure complexity with no present benefit. Revisit only if the A/B test or journey libraries grow by roughly an order of magnitude.

perEntryMetadataAudit.lastModified: hardcoded to build time (`now = new Date()`) for every single entry today - this makes lastmod meaningless as a freshness signal (every entry looks equally 'just changed' on every deploy, regardless of whether that page's content actually changed). Not fixed this round (would need per-record last-touched dates, which none of the current data sources track) - flagged as a real, low-urgency improvement: Google treats an inaccurate/always-current lastmod as a weak signal it may start ignoring, so this isn't harmful today, just not useful.
perEntryMetadataAudit.changeFrequency: hardcoded 'monthly' everywhere - reasonably honest given how infrequently any of these pages actually change; no fix needed.
perEntryMetadataAudit.priority: home=1, journey details=0.4, everything else=0.7 - a coarse but defensible hierarchy (home > general pages > the largest, most granular detail-page family). Google has stated it mostly ignores sitemap priority as a ranking signal, so this is low-stakes; no change recommended.
